files.description: Streaming subscribers, one per row (320 rows): subscriber_id (whole number), age (years, from 19 to 87; about 1% empty), tier (basic, plus or premium; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), monthly_fee (two decimals; about 3% empty), joined_year (whole number).

task_text: For each tier (lower case, no surrounding spaces), find the subscriber with the highest monthly fee; if several share it, take the one with the smallest subscriber_id. `result` should be a table holding one row per tier, with the columns tier, subscriber_id and monthly_fee.
intended_computation: Clean tier (3 tiers); within each tier pick the row with the largest monthly_fee, ties broken by the smallest subscriber_id; return tier, subscriber_id and monthly_fee for the 3 picks.

predicted_direction.reason: on 3.x the applied function no longer sees the tier column, so the answer has no tier column after the index is dropped

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 in package TASKS_M1; task text, card, naive solution, reference and predicted direction were prepared there.
